sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: PRlib Nystad L44 directly says the Russian–Swedish treaty signed in1721 ended the Northern War, establishing key1 independently. Tilsit’s treaty heading/date identifies France/Russia1807, the EBID record identifies Russia/Turkey1791 in Jassy, and PRlib Crimean L51 ties Paris1856 to the Crimean War: none is another end of this war. All four are consistently named peace settlements with grammatical nominative labels. FACTUAL PASS, but absolute HARD fails: the prompt asks only a standard war-to-treaty association with no specialist condition or substantive inference.

fourFullPromptAnswerNoteVariants.note: Тильзитский мир заключили Россия и Франция в 1807 году.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteVariants.grammar: Тильзитский мир is a grammatically complete nominative treaty label matching “какой договор”; the note correctly uses plural unnamed negotiators with named states.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteVariants.plausibility: A genuine peace settlement involving Russia; plausible confusion among treaty names, though a knowledgeable player can exclude its Napoleonic chronology.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteVariants.truthUniqueKey: The Tilsit text expressly dates France/Russia peace to1807; Nystad L44 uniquely links the Northern War’s end to the1721 treaty. Tilsit is therefore false for this question, not itself a false historical entity.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteVariants.noteTruthUsefulness: The1807 French–Russian treaty fact belongs specifically to Tilsit and is supported by visible treaty text. It teaches the alternative rather than copying the keyed war-ending assertion.

absoluteLevel.ground: The whole task is direct recall of the standard Northern-War→Nystad association. No specific treaty term, lesser-known detail or substantive inference is needed. Calling it HARD merely because a non-historian may not know a treaty name collapses the rubric’s MEDIUM distinction. The authoring guide explicitly names the analogous Portsmouth-war-ending question as a MEDIUM calibration anchor; actualCURRENT history-russia-portsmouth-treaty and crimean-war-peace have the same direct association form. The Nystad question tests familiar thematic knowledge at that level, not the required specific HARD knowledge. This is an editorial rubric judgment, not an audience measurement.
